newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1997 deficit 3.0 pct of GDP - govt sources.
newsitem.headline: German 1997 deficit 3.0 pct of GDP - govt sources.

text.p: Germany's public sector budget deficit will total 110 billion marks ($62 billion) or 3.0 percent of economic output in 1997, in line with the target for European monetary union (EMU), government sources said on Thursday.

In its long-term financial plan, the government sees growth rates as moderate but steady, the sources said. GDP growth in 1997 is seen at 2.5 percent, rising to 2.75 percent next year, and coming back to 2.5 percent in each of the three years following.
The supplementary budget for 1997 due to be presented by Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Friday foresees a federal deficit of 71.2 billion marks, up from 53.3 billion marks in the original plan.
But "positive developments in federal special assets and social security" will help offset the larger federal deficit, the sources said, without giving details.
Total public sector debt will be slightly over the EMU target of 60 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the sources said, but will be brought back into line by 2001.
